note.text:
Points are collinear when one straight line passes through all of them.
• Any two points are always collinear, because one line passes through any two points.
• Three points A, B and C are collinear if C is on the line (AB).
To test with your ruler, place its edge on two of the points and see if the third point touches the edge too.

If B is on the segment [AC], then A, B and C are collinear and AB + BC = AC. For example, three taxi stops on a straight road: if AB = 3 km and BC = 5 km, then AC = 8 km.

If AB + BC is bigger than AC, then B is not on [AC].

worked_example.problem: In a small town, straight roads join three places: from {P} to {Q} is {a} km, from {Q} to {R} is {b} km, and from {P} to {R} is {c} km. Are the three places collinear, with {Q} between the other two?
steps: If {Q} is on the straight segment between {P} and {R}, then the two short distances add up to the long one.
The two short distances: {a} km + {b} km = {a + b} km.
The long distance, from {P} to {R}, is {c} km. The two results are {a + b == c ? 'equal' : 'not equal'}.
worked_example.answer: {a + b == c ? 'Yes: the three places are collinear, with ' + Q + ' between ' + P + ' and ' + R + '.' : 'No: ' + Q + ' is not on the segment.'}

cards.idea: Points are collinear when one straight line passes through all of them.
example: Three taxi stops on a straight road are collinear.
A house away from the road is not collinear with them.

cards.idea: Any two points are always collinear, because one line passes through any two points. Three points are collinear only if the third is on the line through the other two.
example: To test three points, put the edge of your ruler on two of them and see if the third touches it.

cards.idea: If B is on the segment [AC], then AB + BC = AC.
example: AB = {a} km and BC = {b} km, with B between A and C.

check.prompt: B is on the segment [AC]. AB = {a} cm and BC = {b} cm. Find AC.

misconceptions.explain: B is between A and C, so AC = AB + BC = {a} + {b}.

solution: B is on [AC], so AC = AB + BC = {a} + {b} = {a + b} cm.

questions.prompt: Points {L[0]}, {L[1]}, {L[2]} and {L[3]} are on the line (d). Point {E} is not on (d). Which three points are collinear?

misconceptions.explain: {E} is not on (d), so it is not on the same line as two points of (d).

solution: Only points on (d) are on one straight line together; {E} is not on (d).
So the three collinear points are {answer}.

right.text: Any two points are always collinear.
Through two different points there is exactly one straight line.

wrong.text: Through two points we can draw many straight lines.
wrong.explain: Through two different points there is exactly one straight line.

wrong.text: Any three points are always collinear.
wrong.explain: Three points are collinear only if the third one is on the line through the other two.

wrong.text: Two points are collinear only if they are close together.
wrong.explain: Distance does not matter: one line always passes through any two points.

wrong.text: Points on a curved path are always collinear.
wrong.explain: Collinear means on one straight line, not on a curve.

questions.prompt: Taxi stops {P}, {Q} and {R} are on a straight road, with {Q} between {P} and {R}. {P}{Q} = {a} km and {Q}{R} = {b} km. Find {P}{R}.
questions.verify: answer - a == b && answer > a && answer > b

c.expr: yes ? a + b : a + b - gap

questions.prompt: {P}{Q} = {a} cm, {Q}{R} = {b} cm and {P}{R} = {c} cm. Is {Q} on the segment [{P}{R}]?

misconceptions.explain: Check the sum: {P}{Q} + {Q}{R} = {a} + {b} = {a + b} cm, and {P}{R} = {c} cm. {Q} is on [{P}{R}] only when the two are equal.

solution: {a + b == c ? 'They are equal, so ' + Q + ' is on [' + P + R + '].' : 'They are not equal, so ' + Q + ' is not on [' + P + R + '].'}
